headline: Producer prices for final demand rose 0.4 percent in August; wholesalers' July sales rose 0.8 percent

items.title: Producer Price Index, August 2026
items.summary: The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.4 percent in August, seasonally adjusted, after rising 0.1 percent in July and falling 0.1 percent in June. On an unadjusted basis, final demand prices were 5.4 percent higher than 12 months earlier. In August, prices for final demand goods rose 1.1 percent and prices for final demand services rose 0.1 percent. The index for final demand less foods, energy, and trade services rose 0.3 percent in the month and 4.7 percent over 12 months.
items.meaning: The PPI measures the average change over time in the prices that domestic producers receive for their goods, services, and construction. Final demand covers sales for personal consumption, capital investment, government, and export, so it is not the same basket as the Consumer Price Index.

items.title: Monthly Wholesale Trade: Sales and Inventories, July 2026
items.summary: The Census Bureau estimated July sales of merchant wholesalers, excluding manufacturers' sales branches and offices, at $801.3 billion, adjusted for seasonal variation and trading-day differences but not for price changes. Sales were up 0.8 percent from June and 13.0 percent from July 2025. Inventories were $958.9 billion at the end of July, up 1.3 percent from June, and the inventories/sales ratio was 1.20, compared with 1.28 in July 2025.
items.meaning: The inventories/sales ratio compares the value of goods on hand with a month of sales: $958.9 billion divided by $801.3 billion is about 1.20, meaning stocks equal to roughly 1.2 months of sales at the July pace. Because the figures are not adjusted for price changes, a rise in sales can reflect higher prices as well as more goods sold.

sections.title: One concept to know
sections.text: The PPI release reports two kinds of change. The monthly change, 0.4 percent for final demand in August, is seasonally adjusted: patterns that repeat at the same time every year are removed so one month can be compared with the next. The 12-month change, 5.4 percent, is calculated before seasonal adjustment, because comparing August with the August before already puts the same season on both sides.
